// purpose: @debuggen/protocol - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root tsconfig.json solution file, which references every workspace project - this one after the four below - so the options here are what that blocking gate (AAP 0.8.5) runs on: a misconfiguration fails the whole monorepo typecheck, not just this package. `pnpm --filter @debuggen/protocol typecheck` runs the same `tsc -b` for this project and its dependencies alone.
// package: What this package is: the single cross-process contract layer (AAP 0.4.2) - the WebSocket message envelope (envelope.ts) and every message payload schema (messages/**), the HTTP route constants with their request/response schemas (http.ts), the session record (session-record.ts), the analysis result (analysis.ts), the protocol version (version.ts) and the transport client SDK (client/ws-client.ts, client/http-client.ts). It is pure Zod schema, inferred types and one dependency-injected transport wrapper: no React, no DOM traversal, no Node builtin, no I/O of its own.
// layering: Position in the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2): shared -> telemetry -> code-analysis -> instrumentation, and shared -> telemetry -> panel-schema, with both branches feeding protocol -> apps. protocol sits ABOVE every schema package because its messages embed their types - telemetry events in telemetry.event, plans in instrumentation.plan, panel specifications in panel.generated - and nothing below it may import it. `references` below therefore names exactly the four workspaces package.json depends on, bottom-up, and nothing else: ../panel-renderer, ../code-analysis and ../model-provider are outside this package's edge list, and a reference to an app or to a package that already depends on protocol is the cycle `tsc -b` rejects (TS6202) and that the `no-restricted-imports` layering block of eslint.config.js forbids independently.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target` ES2023, `skipLibCheck` and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). No strictness flag is relaxed here, and no compiler or compiler package is declared: TypeScript 6.0.3 is pinned once, in the root manifest (AAP 0.3.1). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json, the root tsconfig.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier would all accept comments in a tsconfig file, but the rationale is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead so that every reader gets it. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects to override with NodeNext (AAP 0.3.4). This package is one of them, for three reasons that all point the same way: all four dependency packages compile and publish their dist under NodeNext; apps/local-service and the VS Code extension host import dist/index.js as real Node ESM (package.json declares `"type": "module"`); and NodeNext's explicit-extension specifiers are resolved unchanged by the bundlers that consume this package on the other side - Vite/Rollup for the DevTools panel and the webview - so the stricter flavour costs them nothing while keeping the Node consumers honest. A bundler-resolution program would type-check an import graph that real Node then rejects. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY SOURCE FILE IN src/** - the single most common build break in this workspace: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension even though the files on disk are ".ts", and a directory specifier must name its file: `import { messageEnvelopeSchema } from "./envelope.js";`, `export * from "./messages/index.js";`, `import { PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "../version.js";`. Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design (TS2835/TS2834), because they would break the real Node consumers of dist/index.js. Package specifiers are written WITHOUT an extension - `zod`, `@debuggen/shared`, `@debuggen/telemetry`, `@debuggen/instrumentation`, `@debuggen/panel-schema` - and resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map. tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts", so the emitted bundle is unaffected. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is inherited, so a specifier imported only for its types must say `import type` / `export type`. Both forms occur here: the message schemas need the RUNTIME Zod schemas the packages below own, while the inferred payload types are type-only imports.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/messages/session.ts -> .tsbuild/messages/session.d.ts, matching the single "." entry the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/. It also pins the program's boundary: nothing outside src/ may be an input (TS6059).
// compilerOptions.lib: Widened from the base's ES2023-only set, which exists so a Node-only package cannot reference `window` and still compile. The transport clients in src/client/** need the web-standard globals: the WebSocket event payloads (`MessageEvent`, `CloseEvent`, `Event`), `fetch` with `Response`, `Headers` and `AbortController`, and `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` for the reconnect backoff. Every one of those exists in all three runtimes that import this package - Node 24, the MV3 service worker and the VS Code webview - so admitting them types real code rather than legitimising a browser-only API. Nothing else in the package touches a DOM type. ES2023 is restated alongside "DOM" because `lib` REPLACES the inherited array rather than merging with it: omitting it would silently drop `Array.prototype.findLast`, `toSorted` and the rest of the ES2023 surface. Deliberately NOT added: "DOM.Iterable" (no `Headers`/`FormData` iteration and no DOM collection is walked here) and "WebWorker" (the service worker that hosts the client SDK supplies its own globals in apps/chrome-extension; typing them here would let a worker-only API into a module that also runs in Node).
// compilerOptions.types: Empty ON PURPOSE, and the one place this project is stricter than its siblings, which each declare `types: ["node"]`. This package is environment-neutral - it is imported by the local service, the extension host, the MV3 service worker, the DevTools panel and the webview alike - so with no ambient @types package in scope, `process`, `Buffer`, `__dirname` and `require` are type errors rather than code that compiles here and breaks in a browser bundle. That is exactly the boundary this package's own tsup.config.ts enforces at build time with `platform: "neutral"`, asserted by the compiler instead of discovered in a bundle. It is not pedantry: it is what stops a future `node:crypto` import, or a convenience `process.env.DEBUGGEN_PORT` default, from silently type-checking inside a package that ships into a browser extension. `zod` and the four `@debuggen/*` dependencies are unaffected - `types` governs only automatically included global type packages, never a package's own declarations - and the suites under src/__tests__ import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly, so they need no ambient entry either. A test that genuinely needs a Node builtin belongs in a consumer workspace that already has "node" in scope, not here. NOTES THIS FORCES ON src/client/**: the injected WebSocket constructor must be typed by this package's OWN minimal structural interface (a `WebSocketLike` / `WebSocketLikeConstructor` pair), never by DOM's `typeof WebSocket` - a `ws` 8.21.3 instance does not satisfy the DOM type, and protocol must never import `ws`, which would drag a Node-only dependency into the browser surfaces. Timer handles are `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>`, never `number` and never `NodeJS.Timeout` (which is not even nameable here), because the DOM and Node overloads disagree on the return type and either concrete spelling breaks in the other runtime.
// compilerOptions.outDir: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base anchors all three per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file and not to the base's own directory, so the declarations and the incremental stamp already land in packages/protocol/.tsbuild - ignored by .gitignore and .prettierignore. A repository-level path would be an output location outside those ignore lists and would leak build artefacts into `git status`; tsc must likewise never write into packages/protocol/dist, which belongs to tsup and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at.
// compilerOptions.paths: NOT set: "baseUrl" / "paths". The four workspace dependencies resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map plus the project references below, exactly as the runtime and the bundlers resolve them (AAP 0.2.2). Aliasing to source would hide a broken `exports` map and let the acyclic layering be violated without anything failing - and because those maps point at each package's dist/index.d.ts, which lies outside the `${configDir}/.tsbuild` declaration directory, no output-to-source redirect applies to that target. Each package's `types` condition is therefore a fallback array, dist/ first and src/ second: a built tree resolves the dist/ declarations exactly as the bundlers ship them, while a tree with no dist/ yet (a fresh clone) resolves the source entry, which `tsc -b` redirects to that referenced project's own `.tsbuild` declarations. That is what lets `pnpm typecheck` stand alone without `pnpm build` (AAP 0.8.5), and tests/e2e/clean-clone.spec.ts proves it on a fresh copy of the tree.
// compilerOptions.jsx: NOT set. The base's inherited "react-jsx" is inert because `include` below admits no .tsx file and none exists: the panel and webview React lives in packages/panel-renderer and the two extension surfaces, which sit above this package.
// compilerOptions.noEmit: NOT set, and no strictness flag is relaxed on top of the base.
// include: src/** only, and .ts only. This covers the contract modules (index.ts, version.ts, envelope.ts, http.ts, session-record.ts, analysis.ts, messages/**, client/{ws-client,http-client}.ts) and - unlike the sibling packages, whose suites are colocated - the tests this package keeps in their own directory, src/__tests__/{envelope,messages,http}.test.ts (AAP 0.8.3). That directory is inside src/, so this one glob admits it and no second entry is needed; the suites are deliberately part of the program, so `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to them exactly as they do to the sources. No "*.tsx" glob: this package emits no JSX. Until the first src file lands, `tsc -b` on this project answers TS18003 ("No inputs were found in config file") - expected on an empty subtree, not a configuration fault.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list rather than merging with it, so the build output directories are named again here; resolved relative to this directory, meaning packages/protocol/{dist,.tsbuild,node_modules}. The ".tsbuild" entry is load-bearing: TypeScript excludes `outDir` automatically only when `exclude` is absent, so without it the declarations emitted by `tsc -b` would become inputs of the next run. `include` above already restricts the input set to src/**, which leaves dist/ (tsup output) outside the program; these entries state that intent and keep it true if `include` is ever widened. Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program - `rootDir` above is what rejects one from outside src/. This package has no test/ directory and no fixture corpus, so nothing else needs excluding.
// references: Exactly the four `@debuggen/*` dependencies package.json declares, listed bottom-up so the order matches the layering `tsc -b` walks: ../shared - the id helpers, `Result`, POSIX path containment and the single `SourceLocation` schema that source.open and every located runtime item carry; ../telemetry - the TelemetryEventIngress/TelemetryEvent schemas the telemetry.event, telemetry.tail and capture messages embed, plus the aggregate result shapes the panel-data route returns; ../instrumentation - the InstrumentationPlan, InstrumentationAction and ModificationRecord shapes carried by instrumentation.plan, instrumentation.ready and cleanup.completed; ../panel-schema - the PanelSpec and DataQuery types carried by panel.generated and the panel-data request body. Each type is referenced, never restated: a second definition of any of them in this package is the defect AAP 0.4.2 calls out by name. What the references do, precisely: they order the build, so `tsc -b` on this project (or on the root solution) builds packages/shared, then packages/telemetry, then packages/instrumentation and packages/panel-schema before this project, and reports errors in dependency order. They are not what resolves the five specifiers - the `exports` maps are, per the "baseUrl"/"paths" note above.
